H4_System_Architecture.title: h4_Live: How it works
H4_System_Architecture.description: Welcome to h4_Live—a toolkit designed to make ComfyUI feel a bit more like a collaborative workspace. Instead of one giant file, we use a modular system. Every node is its own separate folder inside `/nodes/`. This makes it easy to add or remove features without breaking the whole thing. The 'Core' engine handles the behind-the-scenes logic while the nodes handle the actual art.
tips: You can delete any folder in /nodes/ to safely remove that node if you don't need it.
Adding a new folder in /nodes/ automatically syncs its code to the UI.
The /core/ folder is the main engine. Don't worry about touching it unless you're writing your own nodes.
tips_and_tricks: You can delete any folder in /nodes/ to safely remove that node if you don't need it.
Adding a new folder in /nodes/ automatically syncs its code to the UI.
The /core/ folder is the main engine. Don't worry about touching it unless you're writing your own nodes.

KICK_THE_GRID.title: (>_<)!! — KICK THE GRID (UI Reset)
KICK_THE_GRID.description: Found in the top-right toolbar, the **KICK THE GRID** button is an emergency tool for when your UI gets stuck. If your nodes stop moving, your wires look 'frozen,' or you just can't click anything, this button refreshes the graph layout and logic without reloading your whole browser. It's a quick way to clean up visual glitches without losing your place in the queue.
KICK_THE_GRID.usage: Click the button if the UI feels slow or wires look messy. You'll see a quick Kirby-style face update as it works.

H4_ModelMerger.title: H4 Model Merger (The Lab)
H4_ModelMerger.description: This is a tool for blending different AI models together to create something unique. Instead of just picking one model, you can mix the strengths of several. You might take the realistic lighting from one and the character style from another. It gives you a lot of control over which parts of the models to mix, so you can avoid making a 'muddy' result. Just be careful with the sliders—sometimes mixing too much can lead to weird colors or glitchy images.
H4_ModelMerger.usage: Use this node to build your own custom 'Merged' models without needing extra tools. You can mix up to three models at a time and see a test image instantly so you know if the blend is working.

model_count.description: How many checkpoints are we smashing together? '2' is the standard (Base + Style). '3' is for when you're feeling greedy or trying to balance out two strong styles with a neutral base.

w_1 / w_2 / w_3.description: The 'Global Influence' for each model. This acts as a multiplier for everything underneath. If you set Model 2 to 0.5, even its strongest blocks will only contribute half their power to the final mix.

settings.description:
Flip this switch to unlock the **'Mad Science'** drawer. It reveals granular weight sliders for every single block of the UNet. 

 - **IN0-11**: The foundation. Affects composition, layout, and large shapes. 
 - **MID**: The core logic and coherence. 
 - **OUT0-11**: The finish. Affects textures, lighting, shading, and style. 

 If you leave this OFF, I just do a standard merge based on your Global Weights. But where's the fun in that?

memory_manager.description: Look, merging models takes VRAM. A lot of it. If you're rocking a 4090, you can leave this OFF. But for the rest of us mortals with <24GB VRAM, turn this ON. It implements my **Intelligent Memory Protocol**: loading models one by one, merging them, and flushing them from cache instantly. It's slower, but it stops your PC from crashing.

testing_mode.description: Controls the internal test generator. When ON, the node runs a full KSampler generation using your merged model and displays the result in the TEST_IMAGE output — this is how you verify your merge looks good without wiring it into a full workflow. It also reveals the seed/steps/cfg/sampler/scheduler/prompt knobs so you can fine-tune the test. When OFF, the node skips test generation entirely and outputs a red 64x64 placeholder image and a dummy latent.

interpolation_mode.description:
The mathematical formula used to blend the model weights. Five modes are available: 

 - **Weighted Average**: Standard blend. Result = Base * (1-R) + Target * R. The workhorse for most merges. 
 - **Symmetric Average**: Calculates a true proportional blend using both models' global+block weights. Formula: R = W_target / (W_base + W_target). Ideal for 3-model merges where you want Model 1's identity to survive. 
 - **Add Difference**: Delta merging. Result = Base + (Target * R). Useful for injecting specific learned features from one model into another. 
 - **Subtract**: Inverse delta. Result = Base - (Target * R). Removes traits from the base model. 
 - **Add**: Direct addition. Result = Base + (Target * R). Same math as Add Difference but semantically distinct for clarity in complex pipelines.

decode_test_image.description: Listen, VAE decoding is heavy. If you're merging huge SDXL models and just want a quick check, turn this OFF. I'll give you a raw LATENT output instead. Saves VRAM, saves time. I'll show a blue placeholder image to remind you it's running 'Latent Only' mode.

test_width / test_height.description: The dimensions of the internal test generation. Default is 512 because it's fast, but for SDXL merges, you probably want 1024 or higher provided your GPU doesn't melt.

clip_source.description: Select which model provides the CLIP text encoder for the merged output. Options: 'Merged' (blended CLIP from all models), 'Model 1', 'Model 2', or 'Model 3'. A merged CLIP often gives the best prompt adherence for a blended model, but if one model has a significantly better text encoder, pick that one.

vae_source.description: Select which model provides the VAE for decoding. Options: 'Model 1', 'Model 2', or 'Model 3'. Sticking to Model 1's VAE typically ensures the most consistent color reproduction since the base model's VAE was trained for its specific latent space.

ckpt_1 / ckpt_2 / ckpt_3.description: The checkpoint file selectors. Each slot loads a .safetensors or .ckpt file from your checkpoints folder. ckpt_1 is always visible (the base model). ckpt_2 and ckpt_3 appear dynamically based on your model_count setting. These are your raw ingredients — the models you are going to blend together.

model_override_1-3.description: Direct MODEL input slots that bypass checkpoint loading entirely. If you connect a MODEL here, it overrides the corresponding ckpt_N dropdown. This is critical for advanced pipelines where you've already loaded and modified a model upstream (e.g., applied LoRAs, patched attention, or run it through another merger). When a model_override is connected, the corresponding clip_override and vae_override slots become visible.

clip_override_1-3.description: Direct CLIP input slots. Only visible when the corresponding model_override_N is connected. Allows you to inject a specific text encoder that matches your overridden model, preventing CLIP/UNet architecture mismatches.

vae_override_1-3.description: Direct VAE input slots. Only visible when the corresponding model_override_N is connected. Ensures the correct decoder is paired with the injected model.

test_seed.description: (Testing Mode) Seed for the internal test generation.

test_prompt.description: (Testing Mode) Prompt for the test image.
test_prompt.example: masterpiece, best quality, a beautiful landscape

outputs.MODEL: The resulting frankenstein Model (UNet). Pipe this into your KSampler.
outputs.CLIP: The merged CLIP model. Don't forget this! Text encoding needs to match the UNet usually.
outputs.VAE: The VAE from the chosen model. Essential for decoding.
outputs.TEST_LATENT: The raw latent output of the internal test generation. Perfect for sending to a separate 'Save Latent' node or HiRes Fix.
outputs.TEST_IMAGE: The decoded image of the test generation. If 'decode_test_image' is OFF, this will be a blue square. Don't panic, it's a feature.

features.name: Smart Decode
features.description: Intelligent VAE decoding. If your test image dimensions exceed 1024px on either axis, the node automatically switches to Tiled VAE mode (512px tiles) to prevent VRAM crashes. Smaller images use the faster standard decode path. If the first decode attempt fails, it automatically retries with the alternate method (tiled vs standard) before giving up.

features.name: FP32 Fallback
features.description: Automatic black-image recovery. After every VAE decode, the node inspects the output tensor for NaN values and near-zero maximums (< 0.0001). If the image is corrupted, it force-casts the latent samples to Float32 precision and retries the decode. This catches the common 'black square' problem caused by half-precision overflow in certain VAE/model combinations.

features.name: Architecture Safety
features.description: Pre-merge compatibility validation. Before blending any two models, the node compares their internal architecture class names (e.g., 'SDXL' vs 'BaseModel'). If they don't match, it throws a clear ValueError explaining exactly which models are incompatible, preventing the creation of garbage static that wastes your time and GPU cycles.

features.name: Mad Science Lab Drawer
features.description: When the 'Settings' toggle is ON, a dedicated DOM panel slides out from the left side of the node. This drawer contains: a Mode selector (mirroring the interpolation_mode widget), a Memory Guard toggle (mirroring memory_manager), and up to 3 accordion sections — one per active model. Each accordion expands to reveal 25 individual sliders: 1 Global Weight (MAIN), 12 Input Block weights (IN_0 through IN_11), 1 Middle Block weight (MID), and 12 Output Block weights (OUT_0 through OUT_11). The drawer scales with canvas zoom and tracks the node's position in real-time.

features.name: Progressive Input Disclosure
features.description: The node's input slots are dynamically managed based on context. Override inputs (model_override, clip_override, vae_override) for each model slot only appear when relevant: the model_override slot is always visible for active models, but clip_override and vae_override only appear once their corresponding model_override is connected. This prevents input slot clutter and keeps the node face clean.

features.name: Widget Banishment
features.description: All 75+ block weight sliders, the memory_manager toggle, and the interpolation_mode selector are banished from the node face entirely. They are hidden using a custom 'HIDDEN_BY_H4' type that forces zero-height rendering. These widgets remain alive in the backend for prompt serialization, but their visual presence is managed exclusively through the Mad Science Lab Drawer, keeping the node compact at approximately 320x220 pixels.

tips: Use 'Symmetric Average' if you are merging 3 models and want Model 1's unique features to stand a fighting chance.
Unlock 'Settings' to experiment. Lower Input blocks usually affect composition/shapes. Higher Output blocks affect fine details/textures/lighting.
If you seek pure speed, turn 'decode_test_image' OFF and use the 'TEST_LATENT' output.

H4_Comparinator.title: H4 Comparinator (A/B Test)
H4_Comparinator.description: A tool for comparing two images side-by-side. It's useful for seeing exactly how a small change in your prompt or settings affects the final result. You can slide between images, zoom in to see fine details, and browse through your history to find that one generation you liked from ten minutes ago.
H4_Comparinator.usage: Drop this at the end of your workflow. It starts in a simple view, but you can toggle the 'Histories' button to see your past renders or 'Inspectinator' to zoom in on specific areas.

image_a.description: The 'Primary' or 'Before' image. This is the control channel — usually your latest generation piped directly from your sampler or save node. It serves as the baseline for every comparison operation.

image_b.description: The 'Secondary' or 'After' image. This is your test channel. If left empty, the node automatically mirrors image_a into both slots so it never crashes from a missing input.

frozen_image.description: The 'Anchor'. When connected, this completely overrides Image B. Perfect for locking a 'Gold Reference' that you want to compare all future generations against without it changing every queue.

save_mode.description: The traffic light for your comparisons. **💾 SAVE**: Commits both images (and optionally a side-by-side composite) to your output directory with PNG metadata embedded. **PREVIEW**: Images are saved as temporary WEBP files for UI display only — they will be cleaned up automatically.

filename_prefix.description: The naming prefix for saved comparison files. When save_mode is ON, files are written as '{prefix}_{timestamp}_A.png', '{prefix}_{timestamp}_B.png', and optionally '{prefix}_{timestamp}_VS.png' for the composite. Default is 'h4_Compare_'.

metadata_text.description: Custom metadata text embedded into the PNG 'Comment' field when saving. Use this to annotate what you were testing — 'CFG 7 vs CFG 12' or 'LoRA strength sweep'. This text persists in the file header permanently.

save_settings.description: Advanced JSON configuration for save behavior. Accepts a JSON object with keys: 'save_a' (bool), 'save_b' (bool), 'save_comp' (bool — enables side-by-side composite), 'path' (subfolder), 'prefix' (filename prefix), 'save_wf' (embed workflow), 'save_meta' (embed metadata), 'save_prompt' (embed prompt). If empty, uses sane defaults.

features.name: Tri-State Selection Workflow
features.description:
Interact with the filmstrip history like a pro. 
 - **GREEN**: Primary reference (Selected). 
 - **RED**: Secondary reference (OtherB) for dual-histories comparison. 
 - **YELLOW**: Persistent Lock (Shift+Right Click). The image stays put even as you queue new jobs.

features.name: Sniper Scope Optics
features.description: High-performance slaving between the Navigator (left) and Magnifier (right). The reticle itself acts as a scope, displaying a magnified 'micro-preview' while you hunt for artifacts.

features.name: Histories Mode
features.description: An expanded 50/50 dual-pane mode. Compares your latest generation against your Green-selection AND your Green-selection against your Red-selection simultaneously. Total diagnostic coverage.

features.name: Telemetry Drawer
features.description: A slide-up panel that reveals the DNA of the selected image. It separates 'Prompt Specs' (Models, VAEs, CLIPs, LoRAs) from 'Generation Settings' (Seed, CFG, Denoise) for easy reading.

features.name: Vault Integration
features.description: Every comparison pair is automatically persisted to the Comparinator Vault on disk. The Vault stores image references, metadata, prompt data, and timestamps. History survives browser refreshes and server restarts. The node broadcasts updates via WebSocket ('h4.comparinator.update') for real-time UI synchronization.

features.name: Runtime Cache (Manual Save Buffer)
features.description: A 10-entry FIFO deque per node instance keeps recent comparison pairs in memory for the Manual Save API. This allows you to retroactively save a comparison you liked without re-running the generation — the temp files are still warm in cache.

features.name: Side-by-Side Composite Save
features.description: When save_settings includes 'save_comp: true', the node automatically stitches Image A and Image B into a single side-by-side PNG with automatic height normalization via Lanczos resampling. Perfect for sharing comparison results in a single file.

features.name: REST API Endpoints
features.description: Three server-side API routes are registered: GET /h4/comparinator/history (retrieves Vault history), GET /h4/comparinator/image (serves Vault images with path-traversal protection), and POST /h4/comparinator/save_now (triggers manual save from the UI with custom settings and target selection).

H4_SmartSave.title: H4 SmartSave (The Vault — +ULTRA Edition)
H4_SmartSave.description:
Welcome to the ultimate forensic terminal. SmartSave is the definitive image archiving and interaction authority for ComfyUI. It's not just a file saver; it's a sentient metadata vault that records the exact DNA of your workflow. It features a high-performance filmstrip for historical traversal, a deep-zoom Lightbox for pixel inspection, and a multi-tiered diagnostic HUD that pulls every setting from your graph without you ever having to lift a finger (or a wire). 

 **⚠️ WORK IN PROGRESS**: We are currently hardening the thumbnail preloading engine. You may experience transient 'Ghost Frames' (desynced thumbnails) during intense GPU load. The core forensic data is always preserved; this is a purely visual artifact.
H4_SmartSave.usage: Drop this into your workflow to replace the standard 'Save Image'. Use the [H], [P], and [M] buttons to toggle the History Bar, the Workflow Parameter drawer, and the Metadata injection panel. It works best when you want to look at everything you've done today without drowning in PNG folders.

images.description: The art. The pixels. The soul. Everything you generate passes through here to be archived forever.

filename_prefix.description: Organization matters. Use slashes like `WAIFUS/V1` to create folders automatically. Supports date codes like `%date:yyyy-MM-dd%` to keep your renders perfectly indexed.

save_mode.description:
The traffic light for your hard drive. 
 **🟢 SAVE**: Commits to disk (Permanent). 
 **🟡 PREVIEW**: Just shows in the HUD (Temporary). Use Preview until you've nailed the prompt, then flip it to Save for the final result.

output_path.description: Optional: Write your images to a specific drive or a top-secret folder. I'll handle all the subfolder logic from there.

author.description: Burn your name into the PNG 'Author' tag. Claim your masterpiece.

model_name.description: The name of the checkpoint used. Essential for forensic backtracking months later.

comments.description: Personal diary notes saved in the image file. 'Lighting was good, hands need fix'. These are permanent.

custom_json.description: Weaponized metadata injection. Valid JSON here is embedded directly in the PNG header. Use it for tracking specific experiment IDs or custom parameter blocks.

metadata_mode.description:
Controls what identity information is embedded into the PNG file header. Six tiers are available: 
 - **None**: No metadata. Clean file. 
 - **Clean (Author)**: Author tag only. 
 - **Lite (Author+Model)**: Author + Model name. 
 - **Lite+ (+Prompt)**: Author + Model + Comments. 
 - **Full (Forensic)**: Everything. Author + Model + Comments + full forensic node data. 
 - **Custom**: Uses the custom_json field as the identity payload instead.

json_mode.description: Controls the sidecar JSON file written alongside each image. Same tier options as metadata_mode. When set to 'Full (Forensic)', the sidecar includes a complete h4_forensics block containing every node's state from the workflow graph, plus h4_telemetry data extracted from the session manager. When set to 'Custom', the custom_json field content is stored as 'custom_dna' in the sidecar.

features.name: Three-Mode Panel System (Sovereign View)
features.description:
SmartSave panels can now exist in three states: 
 - **Docked**: Standard node-relative position. 
 - **Pinned (📌)**: Locks the panel to the screen edge (left 0) and nudges the canvas 340px to the right to keep your graph centered and unobstructed. 
 - **Popout (↗)**: Launches the forensic interface into a dedicated browser window with postMessage synchronization. Ideal for multi-monitor workstations.

features.name: Recursive Forensic Engine (v24.14.38)
features.description: The smartest part of the node. It autonomously crawls your workflow graph backwards recursively to find every single node connected to the image chain. It extracts their current state, widget values, and internal logic to populate the [P] Parameter drawer with zero-wire simplicity.

features.name: Tier-2 Insight Drawers
features.description: Deep-dive diagnostic HUD. Clicking any node card in the Parameters list slides out a secondary drawer containing the full internal state, specific IDs, and raw values for that particular node. Multi-tiered tactical inspection.

features.name: Viewport Sovereignty Protocol
features.description: The node intelligently synchronizes its DOM presence with your canvas view. Elements are purged from the document body if the node is off-screen or zoomed out past the 0.35x interactive floor, ensuring 100% ghost-free, high-performance canvas interaction.

features.name: Lightbox Traveler v3
features.description: Double-click any thumbnail to enter the Lightbox. Now features full keyboard navigation (Arrows), high-fidelity zoom up to 500%, and persistent index tracking so you can trawl through months of work in one sitting.

features.name: Shadow Banishment
features.description: Standard ComfyUI widgets are kept alive in the backend for prompt validation but are physically banished to -9999px in the UI. This grants the H4 Sovereign HUD absolute, unobstructed authority over the visual real estate.

features.name: History Filmstrip (Tactical Nav)
features.description: A high-performance horizontal gallery of your last generations. Use the bottom-left [H] button to toggle it. It's virtualized to handle hundreds of images without lagging your browser.

features.name: FIFO Digital Janitor
features.description: First-In-First-Out logic. I keep the last 25 images per prefix subfolder and automatically prune the oldest files, keeping your output directory clean and your storage happy.

features.name: Asset Synchronization (The RX)
features.description: Unified asset retrieval across Hover, Lightbox, and Canvas Background. By synchronizing every request with the preloader's unique timestamp hash, we ensure all elements hit the local browser cache, eliminating redundant backend traffic and ensuring instant tactile responsiveness.

features.name: SQLite Manifest Cache
features.description: Every saved image is recorded in a local SQLite database (WAL mode for concurrency) with filename, subfolder, type, timestamp, and full sidecar JSON. This enables instant history queries without filesystem scanning. The database auto-creates on first run and includes a cold-boot sync that indexes existing h4_ files on startup.

features.name: Smart Counter (Anti-Overwrite)
features.description: Before writing any file, the node scans the target directory for existing files matching the prefix pattern and calculates the next available counter value. This prevents generational overwrites even across server restarts or interrupted queues. Files are named as '{prefix}_{NNNN}.png' with zero-padded 4-digit counters.

features.name: REST API Endpoints
features.description: Four server-side API routes: GET /h4/smart_save/history (paginated manifest query, default 5 items), GET /h4/smart_save/sidecar (retrieves the JSON sidecar for any saved image by filename), POST /h4/smart_save/cache_swap (stores undo state per node), and GET /h4/smart_save/cache_swap (retrieves undo state per node).

H4_Pythonipulator-inator.title: H4 Pythonipulator-inator (The image Kernel 🐍)
H4_Pythonipulator-inator.description: The ultimate image manipulation suite for h4_Live. It's a high-performance **Hybrid Kernel** that combines Pillow, OpenCV, and scikit-image into a single multi-threaded pipeline. Where standard nodes struggle with memory churn, the Kernel uses zero-copy transformations to apply complex filters (Chromatic Aberration, Glitch, Scanlines) in real-time. It's built for those who need surgical precision without the spaghetti wiring of 10 separate nodes.
H4_Pythonipulator-inator.usage: Connect an image and toggle the effect categories you want to use (Cyberpunk, Geometric, Color, Blur, etc.). Each category has a master 'Enabled' switch to keep things tidy. Use it to polish your results or as a creative tool to mess with your images in weird and wonderful ways.

image.description: The input image you want to manipulate.

operation_mode.description:
Choose the workflow state: 
 **🟢 Passthrough**: Just apply effects and send to the next node. 
 **💾 Save to Disk**: Apply effects and save files to your output folder. 
 **✨ Both**: Do everything.

cb_enabled (Cyberpunk).description: Unlock the futurist effects: Chromatic Aberration for that lens-distortion look, Glitch for digital artifacts, and Scanlines for that retro-CRT monitor vibe.

geo_enabled (Geometric).description: The canvas toolbox: Flip your image horizontally/vertically, rotate it by any angle, or resize it using specific scales or dimensions.

clr_enabled (Color).description: Standard processing: Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, and Sharpness. Also includes Invert (Negative) and Gamma correction for fixing washed-out lighting.

blur_enabled (Blur).description: Focus control: Gaussian and Box blurs for softness, or Median blur for that 'painted' look. Also features a dedicated Sharpen pass for crisp edges.

sty_enabled (Stylistic).description: Aesthetic filters: Pixelate your image for a retro look, or add a Vignette to darken the edges and draw the eye to the center.

noise_enabled (Noise).description: Grain control: Adds Gaussian noise to your image. Great for removing that 'too clean' AI look or matching film grain.

edge_enabled (Edge).description: Vision tools: Canny Edge detection. You can output just the lines (Standalone) or overlay the glowing edges on top of your original image (Overlay).

features.name: Surgical Drawer UI
features.description: The node stays compact by default. Toggling an 'Enabled' switch for a category like Color or Blur dynamically reveals all its associated sliders and knobs. It's professional tools without the clutter.

features.name: Tactical Save Engine
features.description: Integrated 'Save to Disk' logic. You can use this as your final node, specifying custom filenames and output folders directly on the face. It saves files incrementally with 'h4_' prefixes to prevent overwrites.

features.name: Inline Kernel Pipeline
features.description: Effects are processed sequentially in a sane order (Cyberpunk -> Geometric -> Color -> Blur -> etc.) so that resizing doesn't break your edge detection and sharpening happens after your color correction.

features.name: Dependency Sentinel
features.description: Smart enough to know what it needs. On first load, it scans your system for libraries like OpenCV or Scikit-Image. If they are missing, it initiates a 'Tactical Deployment' and installs them automatically for you.

H4_TrafficCop.title: H4 Traffic Cop (Legacy Splitter)
H4_TrafficCop.description: Standard Logic Gates in ComfyUI are kinda... fragile. This node acts as a specific 'Start vs Loop' splitter. It takes one input and sends it to the 'Start' output on Run 0, and the 'Loop' output on Run 1+. It's a legacy version of the Router logic, useful for simpler setups. The node reads and increments the global h4 loop counter on each execution, and resets the counter when restart_on_true is toggled ON.
H4_TrafficCop.usage: Use this if you want to fork a single input into two different processing chains based on whether it's the first run or a loop.

any_input.description: The item to be routed. Accepts any ComfyUI type (IMAGE, LATENT, MODEL, STRING, etc.). The node validates that this input is not None and raises a ValueError if it is, preventing silent downstream failures.

restart_on_true.description: Force reset the global loop counter to 0. When ON, the node calls reset_state() and treats the current execution as Run 0 regardless of previous count. When OFF, the node reads the current count and increments it for the next pass.

outputs.Run_Once_(Start): The input data, passed through on every execution. Logically 'active' on Run 0.
outputs.Loop_(Continue): The input data, passed through on every execution. Logically 'active' on Run 1+. Both outputs always receive data (Safe Passthrough) to prevent downstream Missing Input crashes.

features.name: Safe Passthrough
features.description: Both outputs always receive the input data regardless of which path is logically active. This prevents ComfyUI from throwing 'Missing Input' errors on the inactive path. The node sends (any_input, any_input) on every execution — downstream nodes on both paths will execute, but only the active path produces meaningful results.

features.name: Always-Dirty Execution
features.description: IS_CHANGED returns float('nan'), forcing ComfyUI to re-execute this node on every queue regardless of whether inputs changed. This is essential for loop counter nodes that must always read the latest global state.

features.name: Universal Input Validation
features.description: VALIDATE_INPUTS returns True for all input types, bypassing ComfyUI's strict type checking. This allows the node to accept ANY_TYPE connections without type mismatch errors.

tips: Wire this node in isolation first and confirm outputs before folding it into a larger workflow.
If a downstream node behaves strangely, inspect the exact type and shape of this node output.

H4_TrafficMerge.title: H4 Traffic Merge (The Zipper)
H4_TrafficMerge.description: Okay, so you split your workflow into two paths. Now how do you bring them back together? With the Zipper. This node takes two inputs and intelligently selects the one that matches the current Loop Count phase. It also handles Denoise switching just like the Router. On Run 0, it selects run_once_input and memorizes its type. On Run 1+, it selects loop_input (or falls back to the Universal Buffer wirelessly) and enforces type safety against the memorized Run 0 type.

first_denoise.description: Denoise value output when the node is in Run 0 (Start) phase. Typically 1.0 for full txt2img creativity on the first generation.

loop_denoise.description: Denoise value output when the node is in Run 1+ (Loop) phase. Typically 0.4-0.6 for img2img refinement.

restart_on_true.description: Reset signal. When True, resets the global loop counter to 0 and treats the current execution as Run 0.

run_once_input.description: [OPTIONAL] Input A (Run 0). The starting data for your first generation. Its type is memorized via orbit_set for type safety enforcement on subsequent runs.

loop_input.description: [OPTIONAL] Input B (Loop 1+). WARNING: Due to ComfyUI's graph validation, wiring this directly from a downstream node causes Cycle Errors. Leave this EMPTY and use H4_ImageBuffer in wireless mode instead. The node will automatically check the global buffer when this input is None.

outputs.Selected_Output: The active data stream — either run_once_input (Run 0) or loop_input/wireless buffer (Run 1+).
outputs.Denoise_Val: The active denoise float — either first_denoise (Run 0) or loop_denoise (Run 1+).

features.name: Wireless Fallback (Universal Buffer)
features.description: When loop_input is None during Run 1+, the node automatically engages Wireless Mode: it calls get_buffered_image() to retrieve data stored by H4_ImageBuffer. If both wired and wireless sources are empty, it falls back to run_once_input as a last resort before raising a ValueError.

features.name: Type Safety Check (Memory-Based)
features.description: On Run 0, the node memorizes the Python type name of run_once_input using orbit_set('setup_type_name'). On every subsequent run, it compares the incoming loop data type against this memory. If there is a mismatch (e.g., Run 0 was LATENT but Run 1 receives IMAGE), the node raises a detailed ValueError explaining exactly which types conflicted and how to fix it.

features.name: Proactive Cycle Warning
features.description: VALIDATE_INPUTS checks if loop_input is wired and prints a console warning explaining the Cycle Error risk. The node accepts the input anyway (returns True) but alerts you before the graph validator catches the cycle.

tips: NEVER wire loop_input directly from a downstream node. Use H4_ImageBuffer wirelessly.
If you see a TYPE MISMATCH error, check that your H4_ImageBuffer is capturing the same data type as your run_once_input.

H4_TrafficRouter.title: H4 Traffic Router (The Big Boss)
H4_TrafficRouter.description: This is the big daddy. It combines the Traffic Cop and Traffic Merge into one massive brain. It manages the 'Loop Count' of your workflow. Run 0 (Start)? It routes data from the 'First Run' input. Run 1+ (Loop)? It switches to the 'Loop Run' input. It completely automates multi-stage workflows.
H4_TrafficRouter.usage: The core of any 'Live Logic' or 'Feedback Loop' workflow. Connect your 'Load Image' to 'first_run_in' and your 'Refined Image' (from the end of the chain) to 'loop_run_in'.

first_denoise.description: Denoise strength for the very first generation (Run 0). Usually 1.0 (Full creativity).

loop_denoise.description: Denoise strength for subsequent loops (Run 1+). Usually lower (0.4-0.6) to refine the image without destroying it.

restart.description: Emergency switch. Toggle ON/OFF to reset the global loop counter back to 0. Useful if your loop gets stuck.

first_run_in.description: [OPTIONAL] The data source for the FIRST run (Loop 0). This is usually your 'Load Image' or empty latent.

loop_run_in.description: [OPTIONAL] The data source for LOOPS (Loop 1+). This comes from your feedback loop (e.g., the output of your sampler).

outputs.Context_Out: The active data stream (either First or Loop input, depending on the count).

features.name: State Memory
features.description: Reads and increments the global h4 loop counter on each execution. Run 0, Run 1, Run 50 — it always knows the current phase and routes accordingly.

features.name: Auto-Denoise
features.description: Automatically switches the denoise float output based on the loop stage: first_denoise for Run 0, loop_denoise for Run 1+. No manual switching required.

features.name: Lazy Evaluation (check_lazy_status)
features.description: Implements ComfyUI's lazy evaluation protocol. Instead of demanding all inputs upfront, the node dynamically declares which inputs it needs based on the current loop count. On Run 0, it requests only first_run_in. On Run 1+, it requests only loop_run_in. This prevents unnecessary upstream node execution and saves computation time in large workflows.

features.name: Graceful Fallback
features.description: If loop_run_in is missing during Run 1+, the node attempts to fall back to first_run_in before raising an error. This supports single-run-mode workflows where the loop path is intentionally disconnected.

tips: Wire this node in isolation first and confirm outputs before folding it into a larger workflow.
If a downstream node behaves strangely, inspect the exact type and shape of this node output.
This is the recommended replacement for the TrafficCop + TrafficMerge combo. One node, full control.

H4_LoopIncrementer.title: H4 Loop Incrementer
H4_LoopIncrementer.description: The engine. This tiny node does one thing: It adds +1 to the global counter. But where you put it matters. Place it *after* your KSampler or Save Node. It ensures that the counter only goes up when a generation performs successfully.
H4_LoopIncrementer.usage: Connect your image output through this node. It passes the image through unchanged, but triggers the system to say 'Ok, Run 1 is done. Next is Run 2.'

pulse.description: The trigger signal. Connect any output here (IMAGE, LATENT, etc.) to gate the increment — the counter only advances when this node actually executes, meaning the upstream generation completed successfully.

wireless_reset.description: When ON, the node checks the orbit storage for a 'request_reset' flag set by H4_WirelessResetButton. If the flag is True, the counter resets to 0 and the flag is cleared. No physical wire connection to the reset button is needed.

outputs.pass_through: The pulse input data, passed through completely unchanged. This allows the node to be inserted inline without breaking the data flow.

tips_and_tricks: Place this AFTER your KSampler or Save node so the counter only advances on successful generations.
Enable wireless_reset if you are using H4_WirelessResetButton elsewhere in the workflow.

H4_WirelessResetButton.title: H4 Wireless Reset Button
H4_WirelessResetButton.description: It's a big red button. But virtual. And wireless. Sometimes your loop gets stuck or you just want to start fresh without reloading the workflow. Toggling this sets a global 'request_reset' flag in orbit storage. The next time H4_LoopIncrementer (with wireless_reset enabled) or H4_MissionControl (in Active mode with wireless_reset enabled) executes, it reads this flag and resets the counter to 0.

trigger_reset.description: The big red button. When toggled ON, sets orbit_set('request_reset', True). The receiving node clears the flag after consuming it. When OFF, the node is idle and outputs 'Idle...'.

outputs.reset_status: A STRING status indicator. Returns '✅ RESET SENT' when the flag is active, or 'Idle...' when inactive. Connect to a Display node for visual confirmation.

tips_and_tricks: Toggle this ON, queue once, then toggle it OFF. The reset signal is consumed on first read.
This node is an OUTPUT_NODE — it will always execute even without downstream connections.

H4_ImageBuffer.title: H4 Universal Buffer (The Black Hole)
H4_ImageBuffer.description: Loops in ComfyUI are hard because of 'execution order'. The graph wants to move forward, not backward. The Image Buffer cheats. It creates a pocket dimension (global variable) where it stores data from the end of the loop. Then, the Traffic Merge/Router can teleport that data back to the start for the next run. It eliminates the dreaded '1-Cycle Lag' where your loop is always using old data. Despite its name, it accepts ANY data type — Images, Latents, Strings, Models, anything.
H4_ImageBuffer.usage: Put this at the VERY END of your loop chain. It catches the result and holds it for the Router. The node operates in two modes automatically: STORE (when image_in is connected) and RETRIEVE (when image_in is None — it returns the last buffered data).

image_in.description: [OPTIONAL] Whatever you want to send back to the start. Image, Latent, Text, Model — it accepts everything. When connected, the node operates in STORE mode: it writes the data to the global buffer and passes it through. When disconnected (None), it operates in RETRIEVE mode: it returns the last stored data from the buffer.

outputs.buffered_data: The data being held. In STORE mode, this is the input data (pass-through). In RETRIEVE mode, this is the last buffered value. Returns None if the buffer is completely empty.

features.name: Wireless Transmit
features.description: The core mechanism. Data stored via buffer_image() is globally accessible via get_buffered_image(). H4_TrafficMerge and H4_TrafficRouter both check this buffer when their loop_input is empty, enabling wireless data transfer without physical wires that would cause ComfyUI Cycle Errors.

features.name: Dual-Mode Operation
features.description: Automatically detects whether to STORE or RETRIEVE based on whether image_in is connected. STORE overwrites the global buffer with new data. RETRIEVE returns the last stored value. This dual-mode design means you can use multiple buffer nodes — one to write, one to read — if needed.

features.name: Debug Telemetry
features.description: On every execution, the node prints the type, shape (for tensors), length (for lists), or value (for primitives) of the buffered data to the console. This makes it easy to verify the correct data is flowing through the loop.

tips_and_tricks: Place this AFTER your image output and BEFORE your loop end point.
The buffer is global and shared — only one buffer writes at a time. If you need multiple independent loops, use different routing strategies.
This node is an OUTPUT_NODE — it always executes even without downstream connections.

H4_ImageCompressor.title: H4 Image Compressor (The Compressor)
H4_ImageCompressor.description: Compresses images on the fly using WebP, JPEG, or PNG with configurable quality. Can preview compressed result or save to disk. Ideal for reducing asset size before export.
H4_ImageCompressor.usage: Connect an IMAGE input, set quality and format, choose Preview or Save. Optionally specify filename prefix and output path.

save_mode.description: Preview shows compressed image; Save writes to disk.

output_path.description: Directory to save files; defaults to ComfyUI output folder.

outputs.SIZE: String indicating compressed size, e.g., '152KB' or '1.2MB'.

features.name: Size Reporting
features.description: Returns human‑readable file size after compression.

features.name: Flexible Formats
features.description: Supports lossless PNG and lossy WebP/JPEG.

tips_and_tricks: Higher quality yields larger files; lower quality reduces size dramatically.
Use Preview mode to compare before saving.

H4_StateMonitor.title: H4 State Monitor
H4_StateMonitor.description: Lost? Confused? Don't know if you're on Run 5 or Run 500? The State Monitor simply displays the current Loop Count as an integer. Wire it up to a display text node to keep track of your sanity.

Any_In.description: [Optional] Connect an output here to force execution order (daisy-chaining). The monitor will wait for this input before updating.

outputs.loop_count_number: The number. The count. The truth.

H4_ContextHub.title: H4 Context Hub (The Mothership)
H4_ContextHub.description: Spaghetti wires are the enemy of creativity. The Context Hub is your cable management solution. It takes up to 10 different types of inputs (Model, VAE, CLIP, Positive, Negative, Latent, Images, Masks...) and bundles them into a SINGLE distinct connection called 'H4_PIPE'. You can run this single purple wire across your entire graph.
H4_ContextHub.usage: Place this at the start of your workflow. Plug everything in. Then just run one wire to where you're going. You can even chain them by connecting an existing pipe to 'base_pipe'.

base_pipe.description: [Optional] Extend an existing pipe. If connected, we copy everything from it first, then overwrite with new inputs.

any_A.description: Wildcard Slot A. Put anything here.

any_B.description: Wildcard Slot B. Put anything here.

outputs.h4_pipe: The H4_PIPE dictionary containing all connected inputs. This is the single-wire bundle that replaces 10+ individual connections.
outputs.model: Direct passthrough of the MODEL from the pipe. Returns None if no model was connected.
outputs.vae: Direct passthrough of the VAE from the pipe.
outputs.clip: Direct passthrough of the CLIP from the pipe.
outputs.positive: Direct passthrough of the positive CONDITIONING from the pipe.
outputs.negative: Direct passthrough of the negative CONDITIONING from the pipe.
outputs.latent: Direct passthrough of the LATENT from the pipe.
outputs.image: Direct passthrough of the IMAGE from the pipe.
outputs.mask: Direct passthrough of the MASK from the pipe.
outputs.any_A: Direct passthrough of wildcard slot A.
outputs.any_B: Direct passthrough of wildcard slot B.

features.name: Console Report
features.description: On every execution, the Hub prints a formatted diagnostic report to the console showing every connected input with its type information: tensor shapes and devices for models/images, latent sample shapes for latent dictionaries, class names for standard objects, and list lengths for batches. Missing inputs are silently skipped.

features.name: Pipe Chaining
features.description: Connect an existing H4_PIPE to the base_pipe input to extend it. The Hub copies all keys from the base pipe first, then overwrites with any new inputs you connect. This allows you to inject or replace individual components mid-workflow without re-wiring everything.

features.name: Graceful Error Handling
features.description: If any exception occurs during processing, the Hub returns an empty pipe and 10 None values instead of crashing. This prevents a single bad connection from taking down your entire workflow.

tips: Chain multiple Hubs together using base_pipe to build up your context incrementally.
Use the any_A and any_B slots for custom data types that don't have dedicated inputs (e.g., ControlNet conditions, custom dictionaries).

H4_ContextUnpack.title: H4 Context Unpack (The Receiver)
H4_ContextUnpack.description: The Receiver. It takes the single 'H4_PIPE' connection from the Mothership (Hub) and explodes it back out into its 10 individual components. Place this near your KSampler or Detailer nodes to get access to the models/conditions you bundled up earlier. If a key is missing from the pipe dictionary, that output returns None instead of crashing.

h4_pipe.description: The Purple Wire. Connect this to the Hub's h4_pipe output. The node reads each key from the dictionary and routes the value to its corresponding output slot.

outputs.model: The UNet model extracted from the pipe. None if not present in the pipe.

outputs.any_B: Wildcard slot B data from the pipe.

features.name: Graceful Null Handling
features.description: If a key is missing from the pipe dictionary, the corresponding output returns None instead of raising an error. If a critical exception occurs during unpacking, all 10 outputs return None. This fail-soft behavior ensures downstream nodes receive predictable inputs.

tips: Place this near your KSampler to unpack the context right where you need it.
You can use multiple Unpack nodes from the same pipe — each one reads independently.

H4_PixelPress.description: A tool for making your images look sharper and more vibrant. H4_Mutate.title: H4 Mutate (The Finisher)
H4_Mutate.description: A finishing tool for your images. It lets you add things like color grading, film grain, or sharpening to your final render. You can toggle on only the parts you need, like taking the style from one photo and applying it to your image, or just giving it a cinematic look with a film preset.

enable_* toggles.description: There are 7 of these. They control the drawers. If you want to color grade, flip 'enable_color' to ON, and the color sliders will magically appear. Keep the node small by only turning on what you need.

H4_MissionControl.title: H4 Mission Control (The Flight Deck)
H4_MissionControl.description:
This is the brain of your loop. While the Traffic Router handles the plumbing, Mission Control handles the administrative state. It increments the global Loop Counter, listens for Wireless Reset signals, and provides a central dashboard for your loop's status. It also acts as a pass-through for scheduler signals. 

 Think of it as the conductor of the orchestra. Without it, the violinists (your schedulers) don't know when to start playing.
H4_MissionControl.usage: Use this as the start of your 'Control Stack'. Set it to 'Active' to drive the loop. Set to 'Passive' if you just want to watch.

mode.description:
The Master Switch. 

 **Active (Master Base)**: This node is the Boss. It increments the Global Loop Counter every time it runs. Only ONE node in your entire workflow should be Active. 

 **Passive**: This node is a spectator. It reads the current loop count but does not touch it.

wireless_reset.description: ON = Check orbit storage for reset signal (Red Button). Only works in Active Mode.

debug_mode.description: Nuclear Logging. Turn this on if you want your console to scream values at you.

scheduler_val.description: Input for a Float Signal (from H4_LinearScheduler). Passes through.

scheduler_seed.description: Input for a Seed Signal (from H4_SeedGenerator). Passes through.

trigger_in.description: Daisy chain trigger. Connect anything here just to force execution order.

outputs.Scheduler_Val: Direct passthrough of the scheduler_val float input. Connect this to your KSampler's denoise or CFG input for scheduled ramping.
outputs.Scheduler_Seed: Direct passthrough of the scheduler_seed integer input. Connect this to your KSampler's seed input.
outputs.Trigger_Pass: Direct passthrough of the trigger_in ANY input. Used for daisy-chain execution ordering.
outputs.Dashboard_UI: A formatted STRING containing a live status report: current mode, run count, scheduler value, and current seed. Connect this to any text display node for a real-time flight dashboard.

features.name: Dual-Mode Operation
features.description: In Active mode, the node increments the global loop counter on every execution and checks for wireless reset signals from orbit storage. In Passive mode, it only reads the current state without modifying it. Only ONE node in a workflow should be Active — multiple active drivers will cause double-counting.

features.name: Nuclear Debug Logging

H4_LinearScheduler.title: H4 Linear Scheduler (The Ramp)
H4_LinearScheduler.description:
A mathematical ramp generator. It calculates a float value based on the current Loop Count progress. Want your Denoise to start at 1.0 and fade down to 0.1 over 10 loops? This does that math for you. 

 Formula: `Start + (End - Start) * (CurrentLoop / MaxLoops)`.
H4_LinearScheduler.usage: Connect the output to a 'Float' input on a KSampler or to 'scheduler_val' on Mission Control.

start_val.description: The value you want to start with on Run 0. For example, if you want high denoise at first, set this to 1.0.

end_val.description: The target value you want to reach by the end of your loop. For example, 0.2 for a sharp final image.

max_loops.description: How many runs it should take to move from the start value to the end value. If your loop goes longer than this, the value stays at the end point.

H4_SeedGenerator.title: H4 Seed Generator (Entropy Control)
H4_SeedGenerator.description:
Randomness is a tool, not a master. This node gives you precise control over your seeds during a loop. 

 Modes: 
 - **Fixed**: Always outputs the same seed. Good for testing logic changes. 
 - **Incremental**: Outputs (Start_Seed + Loop_Count). Deterministic but changing. Good for sweeps. 
 - **Random**: Pure chaos. New seed every time.
H4_SeedGenerator.usage: Connect this to the 'scheduler_seed' input of Mission Control.

start_seed.description: Your starting number. For Incremental mode, this is the base — the actual seed is start_seed + current_loop_count. For Fixed mode, this is always the output. For Random mode, this is ignored entirely. Supports the full 64-bit unsigned integer range (0 to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).

mode.description:
Decide how the numbers change each run. 

 **Incremental**: Adds the current run number to the start seed (deterministic sweep). 
 **Fixed**: Never changes. Same seed every time for A/B testing. 
 **Random**: Picks a completely new 64-bit random number every time using Python's random.randint.

broadcast.description: When ON, the node broadcasts the generated seed to ALL other nodes in the workflow via WebSocket (event: 'h4_broadcast_seed'). This allows you to synchronize seeds across multiple KSamplers or other seed-consuming nodes without wiring them all individually.

outputs.Scheduled_Seed: The calculated seed integer. In Incremental mode: start_seed + loop_count. In Fixed mode: start_seed. In Random mode: a new random 64-bit integer.

features.name: WebSocket Broadcast
features.description: When broadcast is ON, the node sends a WebSocket message ('h4_broadcast_seed') containing the seed value and source node ID. Frontend listeners can use this to automatically update seed widgets across the entire workflow without physical wire connections.

tips: Use Incremental mode for reproducible seed sweeps across loop iterations.
Use broadcast to synchronize seeds across multiple KSamplers in parallel branches.
Random mode forces IS_CHANGED to return NaN, ensuring it always re-executes.

H4_Gridinator.title: H4 Gridinator (The Grid Maker)
H4_Gridinator.description: A node for creating grids of images to compare different settings. You can test multiple models, prompts, or things like 'Steps' and 'CFG' all at once. It's designed to be efficient, so it tries to group tasks together to save time and memory. It's the best way to see a big range of options without rendering them one-by-one manually.
H4_Gridinator.usage: Connect your checkpoint and set what you want to test on the X, Y, and Z axes. It will generate a large sheet showing all the variations.

image_upload.description: CRITICAL FOR IMG2IMG. Upload your source image here. If I see an image, I automatically enter Img2img mode. If empty, I default to Txt2Img. Supported: .jpg, .png, .webp.

base_model.description: THE BRAIN: Your primary Checkpoint. For grids comparing OTHER models, this acts as the default if an axis value is missing.

base_model_fuzzy.description: FUZZY HUNTER: Can't find your model? Type a piece of the name here (e.g., 'juggernaut'). I'll scan your folders and find the best match. This OVERRIDES the dropdown.

grid_x/y/z_mode.description:
Choose your dimension! 

 - **Model**: Swap checkpoints. 
 - **LoRA**: Test strengths or different LoRAs. 
 - **Prompt**: Every cell gets a unique prompt. Splits by **NEWLINES**. 
 - **Multi-Prompt**: The **{Brace}** system. See features below! 
 - **Prompt Stutter**: Randomizes your prompt variations. 
 - **CFG/Steps/Denoise**: Standard setting sweeps.

stutter_mode.description:
PROMPT AUTOMATION. 

 - **Permutations**: Splits {red|blue} into multiple cells. 
 - **Emphasis**: Expands [dog*3] into 'dog dog dog'.

sliding_scale_enable.description: AUTO-GENERATOR. Turn this ON to automatically generate a linear range between Min and Max values for Steps or Denoise. No more typing '0.1, 0.2, 0.3...'

features.name: The {Brace} System (Multi-Prompt)
features.description:
This is the king of prompt testing. When using 'Multi-Prompt' mode, I look for content inside `{}` curly braces. This allows you to use commas naturally inside your tags without breaking the grid. I also ignore anything *between* the braces (dots, slashes, notes), giving you a clean visual layout.

 **Example 1**: `{1girl, beach}` / `{1girl, forest}`
 **Example 2**: `{blue eyes}.{red eyes}.{green eyes}`
features.example: Use this to test wildly different concepts on one axis.

features.name: VRAM Optimization Loop
features.description: I don't just run images in order (0,0,0 -> 0,0,1). I pre-calculate every task and group them by Model and LoRA. I'll load Model A, run all associated cells, then swap once to Model B. This saves massive amounts of time and VRAM fragmentation.

features.name: Dynamic Label Sizing
features.description: I measure the text bounds of your labels and automatically expand the grid margins to fit. Whether your prompt is 'Cat' or 'A hyper-detailed masterpiece of a futuristic cat in space', the label will never be cut off.

features.name: SDXL Auto-Safety
features.description: I automatically detect if you are using SDXL models and encourage 1024x1024 resolutions to prevent those weird 'low-res' artifacting issues. I'll even warn you if your dimensions are not multiples of 8.

tips: Use the 'Fuzzy Hunter' for models if you have a massive library. It's much faster than scrolling.
For Multi-Prompt mode, put your prompts in braces `{prompt}` to keep things tidy.
Combine 'Linear Scheduler' (Sliding Scale) on one axis with 'Models' on another to find the 'Sweet Spot' for a new checkpoint.

H4_DataStream.title: H4 DataStream (The Batch Processor)
H4_DataStream.description: This is your batch processing buddy. Point it at a folder or a video, and it’ll feed images into your workflow one by one. Perfect for when you have a hundred pictures to process and don’t want to do it manually. It transforms a static graph into a dynamic processing pipeline.

folder_path.description: Absolute path to your folder full of images or a video file.

tips_and_tricks: Use this to turn a video into a series of AI-processed frames.
The 'Browse' button in the UI lets you pick a folder without typing the path manually.

H4_AxisDriver.title: H4 Axis Driver (The Navigator)
H4_AxisDriver.description: Think of this as your workflow's GPS. It helps you navigate complex grids and axis-based comparisons, making sure every generation lands exactly where it should on the chart. It's the engine behind your XYZ plots, taking lists of values and feeding them into your workflow to create comparison grids.

Use it to find the 'Sweet Spot' for a new checkpoint.

H4_DisplayAny.title: H4 Display Any (The Forensic Monitor)
H4_DisplayAny.description: Stop guessing what's in your wires! This little guy just peeks inside any connection and tells you what's there in plain text. Tensors, strings, numbers—it sees all. Essential for debugging and verifying your data flow.

outputs.output: A pure pass-through of whatever you plugged in. It doesn't change your data at all; it just lets me take a look at it.

H4_DocuScribe.purpose: Keep your workflow documented and your experiments organized.

H4_FaceForge.title: H4 FaceForge (The Plastic Surgeon)
H4_FaceForge.description: The ultimate plastic surgeon for your AI art. It swaps faces, fixes blurry eyes, and makes sure everyone looks their best without looking 'fake'. It combines surgical face swapping, deep restoration (GFPGAN/CodeFormer), and smart occlusion handling (SAM) into one powerful node.

tips_and_tricks: Use 'Preserve Hair' if your character has bangs to avoid that 'wig' look.
CodeFormer at 0.5 weight is usually the 'Sweet Spot' for quality.

H4_IdentityEngine.title: H4 Identity Engine (The Persona Engine)
H4_IdentityEngine.description: A tool designed for creating consistent characters across multiple images. It combines loading, prompting, and face swapping into one node so you can define a character's 'DNA' (their fixed appearance) and then just tell them what to do in each scene.

H4_DoubleSampler.title: H4 Double Sampler (The Mutation Engine)
H4_DoubleSampler.description: This is the sampler that doesn't know when to quit. H4_TheForge.title: H4 The Forge (Mission Control)

H4_Switcheroo.title: H4 Switcheroo (The Universal Swapper)
H4_Switcheroo.description: The universal swapper. Need to change 'Red Dress' to 'Blue Suit' across 5 different prompts? This node handles all the find-and-replace magic for you, even for complex neural network blocks. It's the ultimate tool for iterative design and prompt experimentation.

H4_ForgeMask.title: H4 Forge Mask (The Surgical Suite)
H4_ForgeMask.description: The surgical suite. It’s an interactive masking tool that lets you paint exactly where you want changes to happen. It plays nice with FaceForge to make sure your edits stay right where they belong. Generate, grow, shrink, or blur masks for surgical inpainting with ease.

image.description: The image you want to mask. Usually your latest render.

mask_blur.description: Soften the edges of your mask. High values help blend changes into the background.

mask_expansion.description: Grow or shrink your painted mask. Positive moves outward, negative moves inward.

invert_mask.description: Flip the mask. Useful if you want to protect one spot and change everything else.

outputs.MASK: The final processed mask, ready for your Detailer or Inpainter.

features.name: Interactive Painting
features.description: Right-click the node to open the Mask Editor and paint directly on your generation.

features.name: Surgical Blending
features.description: Combined expansion and blur logic ensures your masked edits never have 'hard edges' when pasted back into the scene.

tips_and_tricks: Positive expansion values help blend your edits into the background smoothly.
Use the 'Fuzzy' brush in the UI for a more natural inpainting mask.
Invert the mask to apply global effects like color grading to the background while keeping the subject untouched.

H4_CompleteLoader.title: H4 Complete Loader (The All-In-One)
H4_CompleteLoader.description: The loader on steroids. It loads your models, your VAEs, and even has 4 slots for images right on the node. It’s the only loader you’ll ever need if you want a clean canvas and high-speed workflow. It inherits all the GGUF and UNET smarts from the Universal Loader.

load_mode.description: Switch between standard files and component mixing (Checkpoint vs Diffusers).

image_1.description: Slot 1 for your reference or source images.

tips_and_tricks: Use this for ControlNet workflows so you don't have LoadImage nodes scattered everywhere.
The UI automatically hides image slots you aren't using to keep your graph tidy.
It inherits all the GGUF and UNET smarts from the Universal Loader.

H4_MultiImgUpload.title: H4 Multi Image Upload (The Gallery)
H4_MultiImgUpload.description: The gallery. Instead of cluttering your screen with individual image loaders, this gives you 10 slots in one compact node. It even hides the slots you aren't using to keep things neat. Tactical batch image handling with dynamic slot allocation.

image_1.description: Slot 1. Click to upload or select an image.

tips_and_tricks: Use the 'Smart Upload' button to fill all 10 slots with one click.
Right-click a slot to reset it to 'none' and hide it from the UI.
The node only outputs active images to downstream nodes, saving memory.

H4_ComparinatorVault.title: H4 Comparinator Vault (The History Keeper)
H4_ComparinatorVault.purpose: Internal service that manages A/B comparison history and cache.

features.name: Digital Janitor
features.description: Automatically deletes old entries so you don't run out of space.

H4_ComparinatorVault.description: The history keeper. It works behind the scenes to save your comparison history so you can look back at what you did an hour ago. It keeps things tidy so your hard drive doesn't explode.
